title: Jewish tradition is no model — Christ rebuked it as voiding God's law
source_text: XXVII. Respondeo, quod ad Judaeos attinet, illos quidem jam olim habuisse traditiones non scriptas. At quales essent & quanti faciendae docet Christus, dum Judaeis exprobrat illos traditionibus suis legem Dei & ejus mandata abrogasse & rejecisse, dumque iis applicat verba Dei apud Isaiam, Frustra colunt me mandatis hominum. Itaque habuerunt quidem traditiones suas, sed Deo improbante, & increpante Christo, tantum abest ut eorum exemplum nobis imitandum sit & habendum pro regula. Quanta vero sit vis traditionis non scriptae, & quam aptum sit medium ad propagandam atque conservandam veritatem, manifestum facere possunt hodiernae Judaeorum traditiones, quas ex ore Mosis se habere gloriantur, cum tamen non sint nisi merae nugae, & impia, putidissima, ac saepe blasphema somnia.
pass_a_gloss: I answer, as for the Jews, that they indeed long ago had unwritten traditions. But of what sort they were and how much they are to be valued Christ teaches, when he reproaches the Jews that by their traditions they had abrogated and rejected the law of God and his commandments, and when he applies to them the words of God in Isaiah, In vain they worship me with the commandments of men. Therefore they did indeed have their traditions, but with God disapproving, and Christ rebuking, so far is it that their example is to be imitated by us and held for a rule. But how great is the force of unwritten tradition, and how fit a means it is for propagating and preserving the truth, today's traditions of the Jews can make manifest, which they boast they have from the mouth of Moses, when nevertheless they are nothing but mere trifles, and impious, most foul, and often blasphemous dreams.
pass_b_english: Yes, Jews had unwritten traditions — Christ called them out for voiding God's law by them.
Isaiah applied: in vain they worship me with commandments of men.
God disapproved; Christ rebuked — no rule for the church.
Today's Moses-mouth boasts show how well oral tradition preserves truth: trifles and blasphemous dreams.
